I found the issue. On line 423, the code does:
```python
path = '%s/' % request.path_info
```

According to the PR description, this should be `request.path` instead of `request.path_info` to support `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME`.

The difference between `request.path` and `request.path_info` is:
- `request.path_info` - The path portion of the URL, not including the script name
- `request.path` - The path portion of the URL, including the script name (if FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME is set)

So when using `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME`, the redirect URL should include that script name prefix.

I understand the issue now:
- `request.path` includes the script name (line 75-76): `'%s/%s' % (script_name.rstrip('/'), path_info.replace('/', '', 1))`
- `request.path_info` is just the path after the script name

When `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` is set, the script_name will be the FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME value, and `request.path` will include it.

The issue in `catch_all_view` is that it redirects to `'%s/' % request.path_info` which doesn't include the script name. When `FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` is set, the redirect URL should be `'%s/' % request.path` to include the script name prefix.
